newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MILAN SUFFER FROM NORTHERN EXPOSURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN SUFFER FROM NORTHERN EXPOSURE.

text.p: Norway's finest hour in European club competition since 1969 provoked conflicting emotions in Milan and Turin on Thursday after a dramatic night of Champions' League action produced an intriguing quarter-final line-up.

Rosenborg's unlikely 2-1 away win over AC Milan ensured them a place in the last eight where they now ironically meet another Italian giant, newly-crowned world club champions Juventus, over two legs in March.

A Milan-Juventus quarter-final would have captured the imagination of two football-mad cities, an entire country and most of the rest of Europe, but few can begrudge Rosenborg their opportunity to recast the script.

As Milan supporters stoned their team bus and hurled abuse at the players, the Norwegians were celebrating becoming their country's first representatives in the European Cup quarter-finals since Lyn Oslo 27 years ago.
Vegard Heggem's 69th minute winning goal made the Trondheim side the most northerly club ever to reach the quarter-finals and a small fortune from their share of television revenue.
Coach Nils Arne Eggen not surprisingly called it "the most important moment" in the club's history. "We played an extraordinary match," he said.
Norwegian newspapers were also ecstatic. "Fantastico! Nobody beats Rosenborg," screamed the front page headline in the tabloid Dagbladet.
"Juventus? Let them come," said tabloid VG. "When Rosenborg beat AC Milan at the San Siro there is nobody left to fear. Now everything is possible."
There was relief in Manchester after United had become the first English club since the Heysel stadium disaster to reach the quarter-finals, courtesy of their 2-0 win against Rapid Vienna.

They now face Portuguese champions Porto, aware they have ridden their luck already. Since the inception of the Champions' League format, no side until United this year has lost three matches and still reached the quarter-finals.
They will also be able to call on Irish midfiedler Roy Keane who is hoping to return within a month following the shin injury which saw him carried off in Vienna.
He needed 19 stitches in a nasty cut, but United officials thought the prognosis would be even worse.
"At first we feared that Roy had broken his leg. It certainly looked like that from the grandstand," said chairman Martin Edwards.
"But thankfully it is only a gash and even though it will keep him out for a few games it could have been a lot worse."
Relief was the dominant emotion in Amsterdam too, one newspaper suggesting a 1-0 victory in Grasshopper Zurich had "brought the colour back to Ajax's cheeks."
The Dutch side's reward for arguably the most important result of their modest season to date, is a tie against Atletico Madrid who are already trying to cast themselves in the role of underdogs.

"Ajax are a great team and a great club. They have a slight advantage over us in that they have more experience in this competition." said Radomir Antic, who conceded his team had at times been outplayed by Polish side Widwew Lodz in a 1-0 win on Wednesday.

Antic will be without defender Pablo Alfaro and striker Kiko Narvaez for the first leg in Amsterdam after both players picked up their second Champions' League bookings. Alfaro is not a major figure in the side, and was only playing in place of the suspended Roberto Solozabal, but Spanish international Kiko is a key element in the Atletico line-up and his absence will be felt.
A further five Atletico men have yellow cards and face suspension if cautioned again.
Antic said he thought the referee got the wrong man when he booked Alfaro, and also thought Kiko -- who was booked for diving in the area -- had been pushed.
Yugoslav set-piece king Milinko Pantic, whose free-kick won the game for Atletico, believes, however, that Atletico could beat Ajax.
"We're the Spanish champions, we have enough quality to win and we are not scared of Ajax, however much of a name they have," he said.
Last season, Ajax stunned Spanish fans by dismantlng then-champions Real Madrid, who were lucky to escape with a 2-0 home defeat after a scintillating display by the Dutch.

The fourth quarter-final will be between Germany's Borussia Dortmund and France's Auxerre, but elsewhere in Europe, it was a day for assessing a Champions' League season which yielded at least one win for every club involved except Rapid Vienna.
Steaua Bucharest leaked most goals with 15 conceded in six matches, but there was plenty of overall pride in Turkey despite Fenerbahce's failure to progress.

Their season peaked with a 1-0 victory over Manchester United. ending the English club's 40-year unbeaten home record in Europe, but the club's Brazilian manager Sebastiao Lazaroni commented: "The important thing was that we came this far. We deservedly won two matches and finished the Champions' League with our heads held high."
